(1) the use of effective distant supervision methods, (2) the integration of a noise-reduction method, (3) the application of a novel entity type expansion method, (4) a novel feature encoding method and (5) the use of a new training algorithm lead to a new state of art for end-to-end relation classification systems on the TAC KB benchmark.

(i) a large number of false positive training examples can be eliminated by simple filtering techniques; (ii) the use of a fine-grained entity model and a large number of training data instances is beneficial for relation extraction; (iii) the use of distant supervision training data is beneficial for relation detection, and the use of distant and semi-supervised training data is beneficial in conjunction with each other; and (iv) the use of entity linking is beneficial for relation classification.

The main takeaway from our work is that

distant supervision can be a valuable tool to train high-performing relation extraction systems, if the training data is carefully prepared and the system architecture is adapted to the specific characteristics of the training data.
a modular pipeline approach is the best way to achieve a high overall performance on the KBP task.
a careful analysis of the sub-problems of a task and their respective quality can help to improve the results of a complete pipeline by a significant margin.
